US Navy UAV Crash, Choptank River,Dorchester County, Maryland

2012-06-11
Shortly after noon on June 11, CG Sector Baltimore was notified of a U.S. Navy Unmanned Aerial Vehicle crash on the eastern shore of Maryland with no injuries. The UAV crashed in a remote, marshy area in between the Nanticoke River and Fishing Bay. The nearest water appears to be a tributary of the Nanticoke River (Langrells Creek). The aircraft was operated out of Naval Air Station Patuxent River. The aircraft was carrying approx 1300 gallons of JP-8 fuel, an unknown amount of which entered the water. The Coast Guard has established a safety zone around the crash site and Coast Guard vessels from Station Crisfield are on scene enforcing the safety zone. The Navy On Scene Coordinator (NOSC), Chris Murray, is enroute to the scene and is planning to hire Miller Environmental Group for environmental clean-up. ETA of the NOSC is 2000 local. No one has accessed the crash site on foot at this time, but a Sector Baltimore pollution response team is investigating surrounding waters with no sign of oil at this time. A command post has been established at NAS Pax River, Hangar 101. Additional updates to follow.
